title: VIGIL plan (plan.json), schema_version 1
description:
One week of directives for VIGIL, an Android commitment device. A planner (usually an AI chat) writes this file, the user imports it, and the app executes it exactly as written: the app never decides anything on its own, so everything it should do must be in here. A directive says WHEN the phone is taken over (its trigger) and WHAT the user must do (its steps). When a directive fires, the phone shows a full-screen pixel eye, the title, and the steps one at a time; each step's checkbox unlocks only after its min_seconds. The user can dismiss early only by holding a button for about 10 seconds, which is logged as directive_dismissed. At the end of the week the app exports log.json (what fired, was completed, dismissed, skipped or missed), which the planner reads to write next week's plan.

Write ONE JSON object, UTF-8, under 1 MB. Start it with a '_readme' string. Keys starting with '_' are comments and are allowed and ignored everywhere. Unknown fields are ignored by the app (the import screen shows a warning for each), so newer plans still load on older apps; do not rely on them.

Some rules cannot be expressed in this schema and are checked only by the app when importing: (1) every directive id is unique across directives AND fallback_plan.directives; (2) every id in bad_day.keep names a directive in directives (not in fallback_plan); (3) expires is after week_of; (4) dates are real calendar dates (no 2026-02-30); (5) the min_seconds of one directive add up to at most 4800 (80 minutes), because a takeover closes itself after 90 minutes. The app also warns, without refusing the plan, when a title is over 40 characters, a why line over 90, a step text over 120, a tier 2 directive has more than 8 steps, a list repeats a day, app or id, or bad_day is missing. A plan the app accepts without warnings is the goal.

$schema.description: Optional link to this schema, for editors. Ignored by the app.

schema_version.description: Version of this file format. Must be 1. The app refuses higher versions it does not understand.

week_of.description: Local date (YYYY-MM-DD) the plan's week starts, normally a Monday, e.g. "2026-10-19". Used to name the files (plan-2026-10-19.json, log-2026-10-19.json). Must be a real date, and expires must be after it (both checked by the app).

expires.description: When the app stops running this plan, in the phone's local time and WITHOUT a timezone: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" (":SS" optional), or a plain date "YYYY-MM-DD", which means that date at day_boundary. No "Z" and no "+02:00". After this moment the app runs fallback_plan, or, without one, its built-in minimal plan (the five prayers, water, sleep), so the phone never goes silent. Usually the next week_of at day_boundary, e.g. "2026-10-26T04:00". Must be a real date and after week_of (checked by the app).

anyOf.description: Local date only, e.g. 2026-10-26: expires at day_boundary on that date.

generated_by.description: Who or what wrote this plan, e.g. "Claude, weekly planning chat". Shown on the import screen; not used otherwise. null is the same as leaving it out.

context.description: A few sentences on what this week is about and why the plan looks the way it does (what last week's log showed, what changed). Shown on the import screen and useful to next week's planner; the app does not act on it. null is the same as leaving it out.

day_boundary.description: When one day ends and the next begins, as 24-hour "HH:MM". "I'm not okay today" mode lasts until the next day_boundary, and a plain-date expires means that date at this time. Defaults to "04:00" when left out, so 01:30 still counts as the previous day. If present it must be a valid time (not null).

directives.description: Everything the app executes this week, in any order. At least one; a good week usually has 8-14 spread over all three tiers. Ids must be unique (checked by the app).

bad_day.description: What still fires in "I'm not okay today" mode. The user can switch that mode on at any time; until the next day_boundary only the directives listed in keep fire, and the rest are skipped and logged as skipped_bad_day. A bad day is not a failure; keep the list to what truly matters. If bad_day is left out (or null), nothing fires on a bad day and the app warns.

keep.description: Ids of directives (from directives, not fallback_plan) that still fire on a bad day, usually the prayers, sleep and one water. Every id must exist in directives (checked by the app). May be empty, though that means nothing fires on a bad day.

fallback_plan.description: A deliberately small plan the app runs after expires, until the user imports a new plan: 3-4 essential directives, ideally including one that reminds the user to plan the next week. Its ids must differ from the main directives' ids (checked by the app). On a bad day every fallback directive still fires. Without a fallback_plan (or with null) the app runs its built-in minimal plan after expires.

directives.description: The fallback directives. At least one; same format as the main directives.

comment.description: Keys starting with "_" (like "_readme" or "_note") are comments for people and planners. Allowed in every object, any value, ignored by the app.

unknownField.description: A field this version of the app does not know. It is accepted and ignored (the import screen shows a warning), so the plan still loads. Do not put anything the app must act on in unknown fields; use "_" keys for notes.

id.description: 1-48 characters: lowercase letters, digits, "-" or "_", starting with a letter or digit, e.g. "fajr", "water-am", "deep_work".

localTime.description: 24-hour wall-clock time "HH:MM" from "00:00" to "23:59", with leading zeros ("07:05", not "7:05"). Local to the phone; no seconds, no timezone.

nonBlankText.description: Text with at least one visible character.

directive.description: One thing the app makes the user do. When its trigger happens the phone shows a full-screen takeover: the title, then the steps one at a time, then the why line at the bottom. Each step's checkbox stays locked for its min_seconds. Completing every step closes the takeover (logged as directive_completed); holding the dismiss button for about 10 seconds closes it early (directive_dismissed); a takeover closes itself after 90 minutes as the active takeover, whatever its progress (directive_timed_out), so all of a directive's min_seconds together must stay at or under 4800 (80 minutes; checked by the app).

id.description: Stable name for this directive, used in log.json and bad_day.keep. 1-48 characters: lowercase letters, digits, "-" or "_", starting with a letter or digit. Unique across directives and fallback_plan.directives (checked by the app). Reuse the same id for the same habit every week so the logs line up.

tier.description: How heavy the takeover is. 1 = nudge: exactly one step. 2 = short checklist: keep it to 8 steps or fewer (more is accepted with a warning). 3 = full sequence, for the non-negotiables; only tier 3 may use quiet "override".

title.description: Headline typed out on the takeover, e.g. "FAJR" or "STUDY BLOCK". Under 40 characters so it fits (longer is accepted with a warning). Must not be blank. Defaults to the id when left out (or null).

steps.description: The checklist, revealed one step at a time in this order. At least one step; a tier 1 directive has exactly one.

why.description: One line shown at the bottom of the takeover: why this matters. Firm and kind, never shaming or contemptuous. Under 90 characters so it fits on one line (longer is accepted with a warning). Must not be blank.

quiet.description: What happens if this fires while the user has quiet mode on (they switch it on by hand, e.g. in class or at work). "queue": held and shown when quiet mode ends. "silent": shown now, without sound or vibration. "ignore": skipped (logged as skipped_quiet). "override": rings anyway, if the user has allowed overrides in the app's settings (otherwise it is shown silently); only allowed on tier 3, so keep it for things like Fajr and sleep.

allOf.description: A tier 1 directive is a single nudge: exactly one step.
quiet "override" is only allowed on tier 3.

text.description: What to do, as a short plain instruction, e.g. "Make wudu." or "Put the phone on charge across the room." Under 120 characters (longer is accepted with a warning). Must not be blank.

min_seconds.description: How long the checkbox stays locked after the step appears, 0-3600 seconds. Match the real time the step takes (about 60 for wudu, 180-300 for a prayer, 5-10 for standing up); 0 means it can be ticked at once. The next step only appears once this one is ticked.

trigger.description: What makes a directive fire. "type" picks the kind, and each kind has its own fields: "time" (a time of day), "adhan" (the user's adhan app announces a prayer) or "app_usage" (distracting apps opened too often or used too long). Any other type string is accepted but never fires (the app warns and keeps the directive). "geofence", "rule", "if_then" and "lockdown" are reserved for future versions: do not use them yet.

type.description: "time", "adhan" or "app_usage". Other strings are accepted but the directive never fires.

timeTrigger.description: type "time": fires at a wall-clock time on the given days, e.g. {"type": "time", "at": "07:30", "days": ["mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri"]}. Daylight-saving changes are handled by the app. If the phone was off and the moment passed more than 30 minutes ago, it is logged as missed instead of shown.

at.description: When it fires, 24-hour "HH:MM" in the phone's local time, e.g. "23:00".

days.description: Calendar days it fires on (the weekday of the date at "at", not shifted by day_boundary): any of "mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat", "sun", lowercase. Leave out (or null) for every day. Must not be empty.

adhanTrigger.description: type "adhan": fires when the user's adhan (prayer-time) app posts its notification for this prayer, e.g. "It's time for Isha". Prayer times come from that app; never put prayer times in the plan. Example: {"type": "adhan", "prayer": "fajr"}.

prayer.description: Which prayer: "fajr", "dhuhr", "asr", "maghrib" or "isha". A Jumu'ah notification on Friday counts as "dhuhr".

appUsageTrigger.description: type "app_usage": fires when the listed apps are opened too often or used too long in one go. Give EXACTLY ONE limit: either "opens" + "window_min" (opened N times within M minutes) or "continuous_min" (in the foreground M minutes without a break). Example: {"type": "app_usage", "apps": ["com.zhiliaoapp.musically", "com.instagram.android"], "opens": 6, "window_min": 30, "cooldown_min": 30}.

apps.description: Android package names to watch, counted together as one group: switching from any app outside the list to one in it is one open, and switching between listed apps keeps continuous use going. Examples: "com.zhiliaoapp.musically" (TikTok), "com.instagram.android" (Instagram), "com.google.android.youtube" (YouTube, including Shorts), "com.facebook.katana" (Facebook), "com.reddit.frontpage" (Reddit). At least one.

items.description: An Android package name: dot-separated parts, starting with a letter, e.g. "com.instagram.android".

opens.description: Fire when the apps are opened this many times (1-1000) within window_min minutes. Needs window_min; do not combine with continuous_min.

window_min.description: The sliding window for opens, in minutes (1-1440). Needs opens.

continuous_min.description: Fire when the apps stay in the foreground this many minutes (1-1440) without a break. Turning the screen off counts as a break. Do not combine with opens/window_min.

cooldown_min.description: Minutes after firing during which this trigger stays quiet (0-1440), so the user is not taken over again straight away. Defaults to window_min (opens limit) or continuous_min when left out. If present it must be a number (not null).

oneOf.description: Opens limit: opens + window_min, no continuous_min.
Continuous-use limit: continuous_min, no opens or window_min.
